column2: Degree adverbs that may stand between the て form and the word of feeling (来てくれて本当に 嬉しい).
Adverbs of gradual change before a ている of なる, which make it a progression (次第になっている, どんどんなっている).
The forms of ある after the で of である (であり, である, であった, であれば, であろう).
Starts of the auxiliaries of supposition that take the predicate before a pause (行く……かも, 来る……だろう).
Kana stems of the auxiliary verbs that follow a て form: いく, みる, くる, しまう.
Starts of the auxiliaries that follow a て form (ている, てしまう, てほしい, ていただく).
Words that follow another word inside one clause and so never start a column: a copula, an auxiliary or a particle at the start of the hiragana run that begins a column.
Particles, copulas and the like that never start a column when they are its whole hiragana run.
What follows だけ and no verb stem (いただけだ, いただけで, いただけじゃ, いただけに).
The copula forms after which そ starting a clause is そう said short (そだね, そであった, そでもない, そじゃない).
The copula forms after a clause-initial そ that make it そう only where the sentence ends after them (あ、そだ。).
The copula forms of copula.short-so-final that also need the start of a sentence, not a comma, before そ (そだった。; not 大きく、そだった, 育った).
Counters after which an Arabic 1 in an idiom of counting is the bare native 하나, as the kanji one reads (1つ残らず 하나 남김없이).
Ends of a word that join its clause to the next one (行って, 行けば, 行くけど, 行くので).
Forms after られ that make the られ of a transitive or listed verb the passive (られている, られてる, られており, られてた).
Forms after られ that make it the potential: negative, conditional, volitional and the polite non-past (られない, られれば, られよう, られます).
What follows the ん of a contracted いる after a particle (にいんの, でいんだ).
What follows the ん of a contracted ている (てんじゃ, てんだろ).
What follows いた as an adjective ending (見ていたい) or as 致す and 頂く (でいたします, ていただく).
The particles and predicates after which a katakana spelling of an adjective reads as the word (ウルサイって, スゴイじゃ).
The sentence-final particles after which a katakana spelling of an i-adjective reads as one (ウルサイぞ).
What may follow a katakana noun: particles, the copula and honorifics (イカなんて, イカを).
The particles and predicates after which a katakana spelling of a pronoun or noun reads as the word (アレは, ソレだ); アレ before ？ is the interjection.
What else follows a katakana spelling of a verb (コロスんだ, コロスから).
Starts of an item that is not a verb or adjective on its own: a copula or particle at its start (で, じゃ, っ).
What follows a noun and never a verb stem: copulas, particles, ある (わけだ, わけが, わけあって), and what also follows the stem of a verb in its own use (わけ、, わけない 分けない, わけは).
What follows a kana verb stem in its own use as well as a noun: the negative, は, も and に (わけない 分けない, わけは).
What may follow a verbal noun that goes on past a counter, so that the number counts its action (1回復した, 1回復を): the forms of する and できる and particles.
Honorifics after which a name spelled like a number is the name, not the number (九十九さん).
Honorifics after a name that the constraint rules find at the start of the text after it (さん, 先生, ちゃん).
The familiar honorifics of honorific.constraint (くん, ちゃん), a subset of it, which the rules about familiar address look for alone.
Titles and suffixes of a person the speaker honours (陛下, 王子, 先生, シンシア様), matched at the end of a word.
Honorifics found at the start of the kana after a name, the longest winning (さくらちゃん, みなみ先生).
Honorifics that fuse with a kanji name into one run (市松殿).
The katakana honorifics a katakana name may end in (ヨウタサン).
Person suffixes that follow a name (さん, 様, 先生), with their drawn-out spellings (さぁん, ちゃーん); a label or run that ends in one is the name before it.
The honorifics that make the hiragana before them a nickname (みっちゃん, けんくん); the last one that starts the text wins.
The titles that show a name to be a person when they follow it (霧島さん, 千歳お姉, 加賀改二).
Honorifics that the rules left untranslated, which leave the spacing to the word after them (魔王ちゃんの 마왕의).
Honorifics read 씨 or 군 that are written apart from the noun before them (田中さん 다나카 씨).
The kin, pet and other words before ちゃん the dictionary lacks in hiragana, which are no nickname (にいちゃん, わんちゃん, いっちゃん 一番).
Final syllables of Korean adjective stems: their 지 않다 is the negative of an adjective (기분이 좋지 않다, 좋지 않은), not of a verb (않는다, 않는).
Korean nouns of 하다 whose passive is the noun with 받다 (사과받다); nouns of neither this set nor ko-noun.passive-danghada take 되다 (고용되다).
Korean nouns of 하다 whose passive is the noun with 당하다 (무시당하다).
Korean nouns of 하다 whose passive keeps 어지다 (말하다 말해지다, 의지하다).
Ends of Korean present verbs that state, not plan, and so are written plainly in 해체 (모른다 몰라, 생각한다 생각해, 마음에 든다 마음에 들어).

Korean verbs of holding, wearing, touching, posture and knowing, whose 고 있던 is the state the action left (抱えていた子供 안고 있던 아이, 忘れていた 잊고 있던); 던 would read as a habit. A phrase that ends in one counts too (이를 악물다).
Korean verbs of actions done one after the other (먹다, 씻다, 자다), whose て reads 고.
Starts of the Korean of 하다 and 되다 in their forms (하, 한, 했, 되, 된, 돼), which show that a する joins its verbal noun.
The Korean endings of a name after which a following honorific is written as nothing (님, 씨, 선배).
Closing brackets before which the space after ? or ! is dropped (정말? 」 정말?」).
Marks of a main clause that is a supposition, hearsay, a degree or a habit rather than an event that followed (しまいそうだった, 崩すほど重かった, 使えるらしく, という欠点).
Nouns that name a quality: the の before an adjective after them is the subject (香りの良い, 面倒見のいい).
Starts of the nouns that need a modifier, the auxiliaries and the adverbial particles that still take the predicate before a pause (行く……ことにした, 来る……まで).
Japanese nouns of declarations and verdicts, whose する and だ keep 다 (破棄する 파기한다).
Nouns after a verb that name the clause rather than a thing in it (していたの, していたこと, していたようだ, 迎えられたこと).
Starts of the nouns that an attributive before an ellipsis or a dash still modifies (行く……ことにした).
Nouns of angle or temperature earlier in the sentence that make 度 one (角度は四十五度, 体温が三十八度).
Speaker labels that name a group, a voice or a role, not a person (みんな, 声, アナウンス, 店員).
Kanji compounds before する that tell a time, a frequency or an amount, and stay an adverb apart from the verb (全部します 전부 합니다).
Nouns before になっている that read as an ongoing state (話題になっている 화제가 되고 있다).
Place and time nouns that start a word after a の the rules left untranslated (가게 안, 침대 아래, 아이 때).
The nouns that a quotation in って modifies (って奴 라는 녀석).
Verbal nouns whose されている is a state (舗装されている).
Words of kinship, address, rank and role: a label or name candidate that is one is a role, not a name (父, 店長, 勇者, マスター).
Nouns of position and situation, after which から and the particle of place read 에서 (後ろから, 現場で).
Nouns of noun.scene that also name a thing one uses: before a verb of verb.means-de their で is the means (夢で取り繕う 꿈으로 꾸미다, 夢で終わる 꿈으로 끝나다).
Ends of the words of time before から, which then reads 부터 (三時から, 昔から, 少し前から).
Words that start with an honorific: after a name they are the title (殿下, 様子).
Particles that may follow a name where a verb or adjective stem would take its inflection.
The case particles after which a verb stem in kana goes on (二つにわけ、, パンをわけない).
Particles after ではない or ではなかった that make a contrast that goes on (大した傷ではないが), which keeps the topic particle.
Particles that may stand between 度 and a word of word.do-angle.
Starts of the word after 程 or ほど that make it a degree (それほどの, 程まで).
Particles that, after the first character of an item, make a phrase that starts with a noun.
The particles a question word may run on with in one word (何を, 誰の, どこへ, いつから).
First-person pronouns whose genitive takes the short form (나의 내, 저의 제).
Pronouns and nouns that end in hiragana, after which a word reads as following a noun (これ, みんな, 予定通り).
First-person pronouns read as the humble 저 or 저희 in polite speech (私はそう思います 저는 그렇게 생각합니다).
Second-person pronouns whose genitive takes the short form (너의 네).
The pronouns and words after which わ is the topic は spelled as it sounds (こっちわ, お前わ).
Question words before a copula だ that ends a quote or stands before 、 (何だ, 誰だ).
Question words that make a sentence-final だろう a question (何だろう 뭘까, どっちだろう 어느 쪽일까).
Starts of words that begin like a question word but are none (何か, どうせ, いつも).
Speech markers inside an utterance that show the speaker to be a woman (ですわ, かしら, あたし).
Speech markers inside an utterance that show the speaker to be a man (俺, だぜ, 兄上).
Marks of old or lordly speech found anywhere in a line (ておる, のじゃ, 拙者).
The classical negative ぬ (ならぬ, 知らぬ), a mark of old speech only before the end of a clause, which 死ぬ is not.
Marks of polite speech found anywhere in a line (です, ます, ください).
Marks of polite speech found inside a surface, which make the sentence polite (です, ます, ください).
Verb stems of the compound particles in て after に, と or を (について 에 대해, によって).
Stems of the honorific godan verbs in る whose polite forms are written with い (くださいます, いらっしゃいませ, ございます).
Stems before い of the predicates of existence, quantity or knowing, whose の before them is the subject (人の少ない).
Second halves of the compound verbs of action on someone (睨み付け, 突きつけ, 投げかけ, 責め立て).
The polite ending and the auxiliaries and suffixes that a verb's continuative runs into as one verb form (余ります, 余り過ぎる, 余り始める, 余りがち, 余りそうだ).
Ends of a speaker label Xの父 that name a relative of the name X (アリスの母).
Ends of a speaker label that make it a role, not a name (サッカー部員, 担当者, 女子生徒).
Person suffixes that follow a surname without being a given name (田中家, 佐藤夫妻).
Plural suffixes that a pronoun runs into as one plural pronoun (私たち, 僕ら, 俺ども).
Title words that may follow a name inside its run (茜たち, 水無月家).
Starts of the する after a verbal noun that make the noun the predicate (回復した, 回復できる).
Starts of the rest of a form of する after its stem し (しない, してる, しちゃう, しよう), not the first kana of まで, なら or たくさん after 今年.
Starts of the する, なさる or できる that join the verbal noun before them (キスしたい 키스하고 싶다, 我慢できない, 購入なさる).
Forms of する written with the marker of 하다 that join the verbal noun before them (即答する 즉답하다).
Starts of Japanese verbs that state (違う, 似る; 高すぎる after an adjective), whatever their Korean.
Ends of the verbs whose て form with an object gives the means or manner (道具を使って 도구를 써서); they keep 어.
Ends of the verbs of filling, covering, deceiving and ending that take what they do it with in で (夢で満たす 꿈으로 채우다).
Verbs that take what they write or call something with と (呼ぶ, 名乗る).
Stems of the verbs of noticing or remembering whose negative takes 못하다 (気づかない 눈치채지 못하다).
Ichidan stems of acts done to someone, whose narrative られた after an object is the passive (決断を命じられた, 罵声を浴びせられた); a conditional of one is passive after its object without a recipient に.
Ichidan stems whose られ reads as the passive whatever their objects (perception and attitude: 恐れられる, 見つめられる).
Ichidan stems whose affirmative られた is mostly the potential (見つけられた, 耐えられた).
Stems that start a verb of saying or thinking, which takes a quotation before it.
Godan stems of permitting, entrusting and taking away, whose subject before the object and (ら)れ is the one acted on (参加を許される, 王位を奪われた).
Stems of the passive verbs whose ている is a state (並べられている, 囲まれている).
Stems of the verbs whose ている is the state their action left, read without an object (濡れている, 座っている); a compound or phrase that ends in one counts too.
Stems of the result-state verbs whose state reads as the Korean past (亡くなっているから 돌아가셨으니까, 古びている本 오래된 책).
Stems of the verbs of talking and going out with someone that keep the progressive of ている in the plain present and in 지 (付き合っている人 사귀는 사람); a stem ending in 言 or 云 counts too.
Starts of the verbs of speaking after a quotation in って (って言った, って叫ぶ).
Stems of the verbs of thinking and perceiving whose ている reads as the simple form (見えている 보인다); a stem ending in 思 counts too.
Surfaces that start a verb of thinking ahead in the clause.
Stems of the verbs of writing, whose てある is what stands written (書いてある 써 있다).
Verbs and nouns of doing something with someone or comparing with something, whose partner takes と (戦う, 結婚, 同じ).
Starts of the words after 度 that make it an angle or a temperature: a change of direction, a bend, a turn, a tilt, or a range or step of the value (百八十度変わった, 九十度に曲げる, 三百六十度見渡す, 九十度近く).
What follows 度 when it counts times: 目 (度目 번째), も and ほど (十度も 열 번이나, 五度ほど 다섯 번 정도).
The greetings お帰りなさい and お休みなさい, which are no orders.
Starts of the words after から that keep (으)로부터 (から守る, から逃げる, から身を).
The words after which であ is 出会う (と出会う, ここで会う), not the copula である.
Starts of the words of company, sameness or difference before which a と going on from the line before is the comitative (と一緒に行こう 와 함께 가자, と同じだ 와 같다).
Verbs and verbal nouns of supposing or describing that take what they suppose with と (仮定, 見なす).
Words of thanks, apology and feeling after which a て or 連用 form gives the reason (어서: 와 줘서 기뻐, 도와줘서 살았다).
